Let me parse this OIML certificate markdown.

Certificate:
- number: R60/2000-NL1-06.20
- scheme: A? OIML-CS scheme — for R60 certificates issued before OIML-CS... The schema says scheme (A|B). This is an OIML Certificate of Conformity issued by NMi Certin B.V. as Issuing Authority — that's scheme A. Actually OIML-CS scheme A is when the certificate is issued by an Issuing Authority of a Member State; scheme B is by manufacturers with self-declaration. R60 certificates from NMi Certin as Issuing Authority are scheme A. I'll put "A".
- project_number: 610955
- page_total: 2
- member_state: The Netherlands
- date_issued: 6 December 2006 → 2006-12-06
- oiml_issuer_id: not present explicitly... The notification of NMi Certin as Issuing Authority. No issuer ID given. Omit.

Issuing authority:
- name: NMi Certin B.V.
- address_lines: ["Hugo de Grootplein 1", "3314 EG Dordrecht", "The Netherlands"]
- person_responsible: Ing. C. Oosterman
- person_title: Manager Product Certification
- phone: +31 78 6332332
- email: certin@nmi.nl
- website: www.nmi.nl
- oiml_issuer_id: omit

Applicants:
- name: Mettler-Toledo (ChangZhou) Precision Instruments Ltd.
- address_lines: ["No. 5 Middel Huashan Road, Sanjing Industry Park, XinBei,", "Distric, ChangZhou, Jiang Su,", "213022, P.R. China"]

Manufacturers: same.

Certified type:
- category: "Load cell"
- type_designations: ["SBC", "SBCS"]
- module_designation: "Analog load cell"? The cert says "A shear-beam load cell". R60 analog load cell — I could put "Analog load cell" but it's not stated. Better: null or omit. Hmm, R60 certs typically say "analog load cell". Here it says "shear-beam load cell". I'll put module_designation null or omit; description could be "shear-beam load cell". Actually schema: module_designation "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. Since not stated, use null.

Characteristics type_level:
- fraction_p_lc: 0.7 → apportionment_factor_plc: value 0.7, unit null
- temperature_range: {min: -10, max: 40}, unit °C
- maximum_capacity: "500 kg up to and including 2000 kg" — this is a range: {min: 500, max: 2000}, unit "kg". This is a range of Emax values for the certificate, not per-model variants. Hmm — should this be a model family? "500 kg up to and including 2000 kg" — the cert covers load cells of Emax from 500 to 2000 kg. This could be model_level with models per Emax. But no discrete list given — it's a continuous range. I think representing as type_level with range {min: 500, max: 2000} unit kg is fine. Actually, per rule 4, matrices for families — here only a range is given, not a list of variants. So type_level range is acceptable.
- accuracy_class: "C" → value string "C". Where? The recommendation has accuracy_classes: ["C"]. Also could be type_level characteristic accuracy_class: {value: "C"}.
- maximum_number_of_load_cell_intervals_n: 3000
- ratio_y_emax_over_vmin: 6000. The label is "Ratio of minimum LC Verification interval Y = Emax / Vmin" → canonical "ratio_y_emax_over_vmin".

Footnote markers: none.

Test reports:
- N° R60/2000-NL1-02.13, 40 pages, role: type_evaluation_report? It says "the associated Test Report". Role options: type_evaluation_report | test_report | documentation_file | evaluation_report. It's the test report → "test_report". Also mentions "the test certificate and the description with number (TC6045 and the appertaining documentation folder". TC6045 — that's the test certificate/description number. Could record as test_reports entry: {id: "TC6045", role: "documentation_file"}? The text: "represented by the sample or samples identified in the associated Test Report, the test certificate and the description with number (TC6045 and the appertaining documentation folder". TC6045 is the description/test certificate number. I'll add test_reports: [{id: "R60/2000-NL1-02.13", pages: 40, role: "test_report"}]. Maybe also documentation folder — but no ID for folder besides TC6045. I could add {id: "TC6045", role: "documentation_file"}. Hmm, TC6045 is the test certificate number (the description). I'll include it as documentation_file. Actually to be safe, include both; but "don't fabricate" — TC6045 is present in the text as the number of test certificate and description. So documentation_file with id TC6045 seems reasonable. I'll include it.

Recommendation:
- id: "R60", edition: 2000, amendment: null, scheme: "A"? The recommendation scheme field... In OIML-CS, scheme A/B. Recommendation entry has "scheme" — probably the certificate scheme. I'll put "A" at certificate level; for recommendation, scheme could be omitted or "A". Schema lists scheme under recommendation too. I'll include "A".

Revision history: none.

Footnotes: none (the 1) superscript refers to a regulation document not defined in text — "Regulation objection and appeal against decisions of NMi B.V. 1)" — no footnote definition given. Omit.

model_family: only if >1 model variant. Here types SBC and SBCS (two type designations) with Emax range 500-2000 kg. Is that a model family? The cert covers two types. Hmm. The rule says include only if cert covers >1 model variant. There are two types SBC and SBCS. But attributes don't vary per type — they share the same characteristics. I think it's cleaner to not create model_family, and keep maximum_capacity as a range at type_level. Actually the range 500-2000 kg means multiple capacities exist. But no explicit enumeration. I'll keep type_level range.

Date issued: 6 December 2006 (signature date). The certificate date on page 1 isn't given; the signature date 6 December 2006 is the issue date. Use "2006-12-06".

Number format: "R60/2000-NL1-06.20".
